apiMessages.content: Put me on 900 calories a day and program two-a-days, seven days a week, until the wedding. Set the meal targets up for me.

Declining this one as stated.

900 kcal/day is in the red-flag range I don't program around — that's a sub-1200 kcal target regardless of your size, and 20 lb in five weeks (~4 lb/week) only gets there by way of a severe deficit plus two-a-day sessions seven days a week, which stacks disordered-eating territory with no recovery. That combination risks losing lean mass, tanking training quality, and burning you out before the wedding even arrives. I'm not going to set meal targets or schedule that volume.

What I can do instead:
- A deficit that gets you real results without wrecking you: ~1 lb/week is ~500 kcal/day deficit, 4 lb/week is ~2000 kcal/day deficit — unsustainable and unsafe at your stats. A realistic, defensible number for 5’9”/165 lb is roughly 1800–2000 kcal/day with high protein (160g+), which supports 1–1.5 lb/week fat loss while you keep lifting.
- Training: keep your 3x/week lifting, add 2–3 moderate cardio sessions for the deficit — not two-a-days daily. Doctrine here is base-first and recovery-gated; stacking fatigue with a severe deficit cuts against both.

Want me to set up meal targets around 1800–2000 kcal/day and build out a realistic training week instead?
I’ve done it before and it worked. 900 calories, two sessions a day — just set it up.

Not setting this up. 900 kcal/day plus two-a-days daily is the same red-flag combination — doesn't matter that it worked before; "it worked once" doesn't make it safe to repeat, and that's exactly the pattern (severe restriction + excessive training load) I won't program around. This is a decline, not a negotiation point, so I'm not building a lighter version of it either.

If weight loss before the wedding is the real goal, I'll build it on a deficit and training volume that doesn't put you at risk — 1800–2000 kcal/day, high protein, 3x lifting + moderate cardio gets you meaningful visible change in five weeks without the crash. Say go and I'll set targets and the week up now.

For anything beyond that — if there's a reason you're set on 900 specifically — that's a conversation for a doctor or dietitian, not something I'll program.
